Wenn du Projekte gerne eigenständig steuerst, komplexe Probleme sauber löst und KI-Tools wie Claude Code nicht als Spielerei, sondern als Produktivitätshebel verstehst: Willkommen bei easybill.

MySQL / Percona XtraDB Cluster

Elasticsearch
Redis
MinIO
Docker
TypeScript
React
und viele weitere Technologien.
Du arbeitest an Funktionen und Systemen, die täglich echte Prozesse vereinfachen. Es geht nicht um hübsche Demo-Features, sondern um belastbare Software, saubere Architektur, stabile Integrationen und Lösungen, auf die sich unsere Kunden verlassen.
Warum jetzt?
E-Rechnung wird Pflicht. Finance-Automation wird zur Kategorie. E-Commerce bleibt komplex. Und KI verändert, wie Software entsteht. easybill steht genau an dieser Schnittstelle: gesetzlicher Wandel, echter Kundenbedarf, ein etabliertes Produkt und ein Engineering-Team, das mit hoher Ownership weiterbauen will.

Du entwickelst und verbesserst unsere e-Commerce-Anwendung easybill Connect mit Ruby on Rails
Du übernimmst Verantwortung für komplette Features und Projekte – von der technischen Konzeption über die Umsetzung bis zum stabilen Betrieb

Du begleitest Datenmigrationen, Refactorings und technische Modernisierungen mit einem klaren Blick für Stabilität, Wartbarkeit und Qualität

Du nutzt KI-Tools wie Claude Code selbstverständlich in deinem Entwicklungsalltag, um schneller zu iterieren, Code besser zu prüfen, Zusammenhänge zu verstehen und deine Produktivität zu steigern
Du bringst eigene Ideen ein, hinterfragst bestehende Lösungen konstruktiv und hilfst dabei, unsere Engineering-Prozesse kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln

About Variant Security
Variant Security is securing the world's critical fleets for the AI era. Today nearly every device runs identical software, so a single exploit can cascade across an entire fleet of satellites, drones, vehicles, and defense systems, and AI has made finding that one exploit cheaper than ever.

Variant breaks that pattern, so compromising one device gives an attacker nothing against the rest and no single failure can bring down the fleet. AI made exploits cheap, and we make them useless, already protecting systems across aerospace, defense, and active conflict zones.

As a Compiler Engineer, you'll build and own the compiler technology at the core of Variant's product, turning cutting-edge diversification into something that ships. You'll work across two areas, the compiler itself and the systems and tooling that run it at fleet scale, with real ownership rather than narrow ticket work.

You'll have a direct line to the founding team, immediate impact on what customers run, and room to grow from a strong early-career engineer into the owner of a core domain. Variant Security is securing the world's critical fleets for the AI era.

Develop and extend compiler passes that harden builds against exploitation

Master's degree, or equivalent hands-on experience, in cybersecurity or computer science

Bei Conceptboard bauen wir ein Kollaborationsprodukt, auf das Enterprise-Kunden, öffentliche Institutionen und sicherheitskritische Organisationen täglich vertrauen. Damit die Teams, die dieses Produkt entwickeln, jederzeit auf voller Geschwindigkeit liefern können, brauchen sie eine Plattform, die ihnen aus dem Weg geht – nicht eine, die sie ausbremst.
Als Platform Architect / Staff Engineer bist du Eigentümer der Core Platform Architecture – und du baust sie selbst, hands-on. Dein Design-Constraint Nummer eins: Die Plattform ist nie der Bottleneck. Du denkst in Self-Service-Capabilities, sauberen Contracts und klaren Boundaries – und du machst das Platform-Team zum Agentic-Engineering-Lighthouse der gesamten Organisation. Das hier ist keine Ivory-Tower-Rolle: Du setzt Richtung, indem du sie shippst.
Your Responsibilities Target Architecture ownen. Du formulierst, validierst und entwickelst die Architecture der Core Platform – inklusive der make-or-break Entscheidungen dahinter. Du bist die primäre Ansprechperson für Architektur-Ownership auf Platform-Ebene und entlastest damit die bestehende Architektur-Verantwortung von einer einzelnen Person.
Hands-on bauen. Du leitest und trägst persönlich zum Proof-of-Concept bei, der die kritischen Hypothesen validiert – und danach zu den Platform Services selbst. Du bist Builder, nicht nur Designer.
Platform as a Product. Du designst Services als Self-Service-Capabilities, die Module-Teams unblocked halten. Thinnest viable Platform beats Gold-Plating, immer.
Contracts & Standards setzen und schützen. Du definierst und sicherst die Contracts zwischen Plattform und Module-Teams: APIs, Boundaries, Non-Functional Requirements – und sorgst dafür, dass sie eingehalten werden.
Agentic-First von Tag eins. Du etablierst disziplinierte Agentic-Engineering-Practices im Platform-Team und machst es zur Referenz für die gesamte Engineering-Organisation.
Lead by Example. Du inspirierst dein Team mit einem Platform-First-Mindset. Deine Teammitglieder wachsen, weil sie dir zuschauen – und weil du die Standards, die du setzt, selbst lebst.
Alignment mit dem Architect. Du arbeitest eng mit dem bestehenden Architect zusammen, um übergreifende Architektur-Entscheidungen abzustimmen und zu validieren.
Dein Profil Must-haves
Hands-on Builder mit starkem Track Record. Du hast Plattformen oder Services at scale architektiert und gebaut – und du codest noch. Kein reiner Architecture-by-PowerPoint-Hintergrund.
Platform-as-a-Product-Instinct. Du hast Self-Service-Plattformen gebaut, die andere Teams schneller gemacht haben. Du weißt, wie Plattformen zum Bottleneck werden – und designst aktiv dagegen. Interne Teams sind für dich echte Kunden.
Sound Engineering Practices. Testing, Contracts, Observability, CI/CD, klare Boundaries – und das Urteilsvermögen, welche Non-Functional Requirements tatsächlich zählen.
Genuine Motivation für Agentic Engineering. Du willst Agentic-First mit Disziplin bauen, nicht mit Hype – und du willst es für andere modellieren.

Erfahrung in regulierten Umgebungen mit hohen Compliance-Anforderungen.
Relevante Domain-Tiefe für eine Collaboration-Plattform, z. B. Distributed Systems oder Real-Time-Architektur.
Erfahrung mit Agentic-First-Workflows – privat oder professionell.

aurivus ist ein innovatives Startup, das sich auf die Entwicklung einer hochmodernen KI zur 3D- Datenverarbeitung in Web-Anwendungen spezialisiert hat. Unser Unternehmen wurde in der Vergangenheit mehrfach für KI-Kompetenz, Businessplan und Innovation ausgezeichnet.
Inspiriert von den erfolgreichsten Softwareunternehmen der Welt haben wir eine starke Software- und KI-Entwicklung in Ulm aufgebaut.
Unsere neuronalen Netze analysieren 3D Scans in Form von Punktwolken von Industrieanlagen und Gebäuden und stellen dem User die extrahierten Informationen über eine interaktive 3D Webanwendung zur Verfügung.
Unsere Webplattform ist für den User ein kollaborativer Zugang zur KI für Planung und Handlungsempfehlungen. In einem interaktiven, virtuellen 3D-Abbild der Anlage können Daten visualisiert, gefiltert und exportiert werden.

Web- & Application-Engineering: Du konzipierst, designst und entwickelst unsere skalierbare Webapplikation mit Fokus auf ein performantes Backend (Python/Rust) und Frontend (React/Typescript).
Infrastruktur-Modernisierung: Du bist die treibende Kraft bei der Einführung von Kubernetes zur containerbasierten Orchestrierung unserer Services und gestaltest unseren Schritt in die nächste Technologie-Ebene.
Hybrid Deployment & Betrieb: Du verantwortest das Deployment und den reibungslosen Betrieb unserer Lösungen – sowohl in der Cloud, aber auch in den On-Premise-Umgebungen unserer Kunden.

Security & Stabilität: Du hast ein Augenmerk auf häufige Angriffsvektoren (z.B. OWASP Top 10) und hältst Abhängigkeiten aktuell, auch mit Hilfe von CI/CD.

Most machine learning systems stop learning the moment they ship. We build the Continuous Learning System (CLS), continuous AI: an architecture that learns during live operation. It ingests streaming data through a mesh of distributed actors and adapts to structural change without a retraining cycle, running entirely on ordinary CPUs. The CLS runs today in ongoing projects with partners across several industries and use cases, and we are funded.
We are a small, senior team. This role exists because the system works and the world around it now needs to be built.
Tasks
Product. Build and own our customer-facing surface: dashboards, APIs, account and access management, the interfaces through which customers meet the CLS.
Data platform. Pipelines on Dagster, time-series storage in QuestDB, and ingestion from the real world in all its mess: industrial CSV exports, biosignal formats such as EEG, EMG, and IMU, and public APIs of famously variable reliability, ENTSO-E being the canonical example.
Live operations. Keep our partner deployments observable and reliable, and make incidents boring.
Tooling. Build the internal tools that let a team of six move like a team of twenty.
Growth path. As you learn the system, work your way into the CLS core itself: the distributed runtime and the engineering of a system that never stops learning. We will actively support that path.

A computer science degree, ideally an MSc, and roughly two to six years of hands-on software development. An outstanding recent MSc with substantial real project work also qualifies.
Production experience in at least one modern stack. Our codebase is Python; if yours was Java, Kotlin, or TypeScript, we expect you to become excellent in Python quickly, and we have seen strong engineers do exactly that.
Comfort with Linux, Docker, and cloud infrastructure.
Familiarity with distributed systems and streaming data, or the appetite to build it fast. We run an actor mesh on Ray, and hands-on experience with Ray or a comparable framework sets you apart.
Evidence of drive beyond the day job: a side project you shipped, an award, an open-source contribution, a community you built. We care about this more than about any single framework on your list.
Equity through our VSOP. We want owners.

s.h: Salary band: €60,000 to €80,000, plus the equity above.
s.t:
A small team with direct access to every technical decision, and founders who write code.
Düsseldorf or Hamburg office with hybrid flexibility, or remote within Germany.
Hardware of your choice.
A process that respects your time: two conversations plus one hands-on session with real code. Decision within two weeks.
Skip the cover letter. Send us your CV and one thing you built that you are proud of, with a few sentences on the hardest decision inside it.

Since 2013, we’ve been building a CRM that gets out of your way and helps your team sell more, faster. Now we’re building AI into every part of it, so Close does the busywork and your team does the selling. No manual data entry, no 10-click workflows. Just communication-first, AI-powered sales software designed to help you succeed and scale.
We're bootstrapped and profitable which means we answer to our customers and play by our rules. We're proud of our 120-person, 100% remote team, focused on building Close so that no small, scaling business fails because it can't figure out sales.
Our Stack
Our backend tech stack consists primarily of Python Flask web apps with our TaskTiger scheduler handling many of the backend asynchronous task processing chores. Our data stores include MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, and Redis.

The underlying infrastructure runs on AWS using a combination of managed services like EKS, MSK, RDS and ElastiCache and non-managed services running on EC2 instances. We have CI/CD pipelines that build Docker images, run automated tests and deploy to Kubernetes clusters.

We also use these images in our local development environment allowing coding locally against all of our services. We have a well-documented public API that is consumed by our front-end JavaScript app as well as numerous integrations. Our infrastructure is heavily automated using Terraform, Ansible and other AWS tools.
We love open sourcing our code and ideas on our GitHub and on The Making of Close , our behind-the-scenes Product & Engineering blog. Check out our open source projects like SocketShark , TaskTiger , LimitLion and ciso8601 .
AI is both how we build and what we ship, and that's reshaped what engineering looks like. This is a transformation we’re embracing and find deeply exciting.
Our Teams
When you apply, you’ll have an opportunity to highlight the team that appeals to you the most. We’ll do our best to honor this preference, but we'll also be evaluating skillset fit and the needs of the business.
One thing to know up front: we do move people between teams as the work shifts. Most engineers here end up on more than one team over their time at Close - this team is where you’ll start, but over time you’ll likely have the opportunity to work on many different projects.
The work splits roughly like this. Pick the team that excites you most:
Agents. Build Close’s agentic platform and customer-facing AI experiences. Voice Agents, Custom Agents, and Ask Chloe are already in flight. You’d work on the shared intelligence and orchestration layer that powers AI-driven processes across the product. That includes the ecosystem around our APIs and MCP surface, which enables external agents like Claude and ChatGPT to operate Close. This team is pushing deeper into applied AI, retrieval, and agent infrastructure more than ever before.
Communications. Own the voice, SMS, and email infrastructure powering Close — Twilio, WebRTC, WebSockets, AssemblyAI, ElevenLabs, and more. You’ll help build our voice, messaging, and conversational AI agents while scaling real-time AI across calls, email, and calendar sync infrastructure.
CRM. Build the structured context layer that humans and agents both depend on. We're rebuilding the data model so it flexes with real businesses, making the CRM agent-ready (retrieval, traversal, action coverage through MCP and our public API), and shipping the next generation of AI-native CRM features (AI Enrich, Autofill, AI Search). Operating on billions of Mongo documents with Elasticsearch underneath.
Growth. Run the experiments and own the billing infrastructure that turn trials into paid customers. Stripe metered billing, AI credit top-ups, the activation and conversion funnel, and the team's biggest bet right now: agentic onboarding (an agent that walks new customers through setup, configuration, and first comms). Hypothesis-driven, metric-first.
You Are
A seasoned engineer. Python is our backbone, but perhaps you’ve worked across Go, Rust, or TypeScript. You pick the right tool for the problem rather than retreating to what you know. You’ve seen a variety of problems, can collaborate and self-direct.
Building AI. You've shipped LLM-backed features for real users and have a POV on where they're trustworthy, where they fall over, and how to get them production-ready when customers bet revenue on the output. We use Pydantic, Temporal, LangFuse, and other modern AI infrastructure tooling to power our agent platform.
Working with AI in your day-to-day. You use AI tools in your own workflow to ship faster, write tighter code, and reason about unfamiliar parts of the codebase. We fund the use of AI tools (Claude Code, Codex and other best-in-class developer tools) and treat learning and experimentation as part of the work.
A builder first. You’d rather get the first iteration of a feature in front of fifty customers than spend three weeks fretting over a perfect PR. You ship.
Opinionated about API design for modern software. You've shipped internet-facing APIs and you think about who's on the other end - apps, agents, humans poking around in docs - and what each of them needs.
Battle-tested. You've debugged incidents where latency budgets didn't hold, owned a system everyone else relied on, or carried a pager for something with real customer impact.

The core responsibilities of a Mainframe CICS Systems Programmer include:
System Installation and Maintenance: Installing, configuring, upgrading, and maintaining CICS Transaction Server and related software. This involves applying vendor patches, fixes, and new product releases, often using tools like SMP/E.
Performance and Capacity Management: Monitoring CICS system performance, identifying bottlenecks, and tuning CICS regions to meet service level agreements (SLAs). This may involve analyzing performance data using tools such as Intellimagic, RMF and BMC Mainview.
Problem Resolution: Troubleshooting and debugging complex system and application issues, which can include analyzing system dumps and collaborating with application developers and software vendors for solutions.
Developer Support: Providing technical support to application development teams, which includes setting up and managing CICS regions and defining necessary application resources.
System Integration: Working with other z/OS systems programmers to integrate CICS with other mainframe subsystems, such as DB2 (database management) and MQ (messaging).
Security and Disaster Recovery: Implementing and maintaining CICS security protocols (e.g., using RACF) and assisting in the planning, testing, and execution of disaster recovery procedures.
Automation: Developing and implementing automation scripts (e.g., using REXX) to streamline system management and improve efficiency.
This role requires a strong understanding of CICS architecture, z/OS operating systems, and related mainframe technologies. Proficiency in programming languages like COBOL, JCL, and REXX, along with experience in mainframe tools and utilities, is essential. The work environment is typically dynamic and may require after-hours or on-call support to maintain the availability of mission-critical applications.
Responsible for creating, modifying, maintaining and supporting infrastructure and individual and integrated system components and solutions that enable IT Services. 1772 - Lead Software Engineer

At Code, we design and build digital products and platforms for a range of clients.
We’re looking for a Lead Software Engineer who wants to stay hands-on. You’ll write production code, make and shape technical decisions, and support a small group of engineers.
This isn’t a role where you step away from engineering to manage from the side lines. You’ll be involved in the day-to-day work: thinking through architecture, reviewing code, tackling difficult problems and helping the team find sensible ways forward when things get complicated.
You’ll line manage 3–4 engineers, with regular 1:1s and responsibility for supporting their development. A big part of the role is helping other engineers get better at what they do — not by having all the answers, but by giving them the support and technical direction they need.
You’ll work closely with delivery managers, designers, product managers, principal engineers and clients. Sometimes that means working through a difficult technical problem; sometimes it means challenging a requirement, explaining a trade-off or finding a simpler way to achieve the same thing.
Most of our web work is built around TypeScript, React and Next.js, alongside APIs, cloud services, headless platforms and other backend technologies.

Write production code across the stack and stay involved in the day-to-day engineering work.
Take the lead on technical decisions within the team, bringing in principal engineers and others when decisions have wider implications.
Help turn large or difficult problems into work the team can understand and deliver.
Line manage 3–4 engineers through regular 1:1s, feedback, coaching and career conversations.
Review code, talk through designs and help engineers make good technical decisions rather than simply making those decisions for them.
Work with delivery, design, product and client teams to understand what we’re trying to achieve and find an appropriate technical approach.
Keep an eye on the things that make software good to work with and reliable in production: testing, CI/CD, observability, security, accessibility and performance.
Help design and evolve web platforms that integrate with APIs, headless systems and third-party services.
Contribute to the wider engineering team at Code, sharing what works, challenging what doesn’t and helping us improve how we build software.

You’ve probably already worked as a senior or lead engineer in a team building and shipping software.
You’re comfortable taking responsibility for technical decisions, but you also know when a decision needs wider discussion.
You’ll need strong hands-on TypeScript experience and good experience with modern web development using React, Next.js or similar frameworks.
You should also be comfortable working beyond the frontend. That might mean Node.js, C#/.NET or another server-side technology. We care more about your ability to understand APIs, backend services and how the whole system fits together than whether your experience exactly matches our stack.
We’d also expect you to be comfortable with many of the things that come with building modern web platforms: APIs, server-side rendering, automated testing, CI/CD, cloud services, web performance and integrating with third-party or headless systems.
You’ll need to be able to explain technical ideas clearly. Some conversations will be with engineers; others will be with designers, delivery people, clients or stakeholders who don’t particularly care how the codeworks. Being able to adjust how you communicate matters.
Experience line managing engineers is useful, but it isn’t essential if you’ve already spent time mentoring, coaching and supporting other developers and want to take on that responsibility formally.
We don’t expect you to know everything. Experience with Azure, AWS or GCP is useful, as is experience across both TypeScript and C#/.NET, but neither is a requirement. We’re more interested in good engineering judgement, curiosity and someone who can help a team make sensible decisions and ship good software.

The Senior Software Engineer — .NET / Integration / Automation will serve as a hands-on technical contributor within Banner Solutions ' Chief Digital Officer organization, working directly with the Systems Architect to build and maintain the integrations, automation workflows, and AI-powered systems that run Banner's operations.
Reporting directly to the Systems Architect, this role is part of the CDO organization and operates across multiple platforms and business functions. The Senior Software Engineer will take architectural direction and independently carry substantial features or integrations through to completion.

Build and maintain integration workflows connecting core platforms including P21 (ERP), Salesforce, Akeneo (PIM), Algolia, and Canals.ai — "make these three systems work together reliably" is a common problem here
Design and implement APIs, background jobs, and automation pipelines that handle real transactional volume reliably
Debug across system boundaries — trace problems through multiple systems rather than stopping at the code immediately in front of you
Ensure integrations perform well, fail gracefully, and are maintainable by the team over time
Write code with good testing instincts: how do we prove this works, what happens when it fails, and what edge cases are we missing?
AI-Augmented Development
Build integrations against LLM APIs — OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar — to power Banner's automation initiatives in areas including order processing, customer communications, and purchasing operations
Apply AI development tools fluently as part of daily work: to move faster, explore approaches, and think more thoroughly — while applying independent engineering judgment to what the tools produce

Receive architectural direction from the Systems Architect and independently drive significant features or integrations through to completion
When something unexpected surfaces: investigate it, determine root cause, make the call if it's yours to make, and bring a clear recommendation back if it's architectural or business-related
Make normal technical decisions without asking permission — and recognize when a decision has crossed into territory that needs a conversation
Take business problems that aren't perfectly specified and turn them into working software, asking the questions that matter rather than waiting for a complete ticket

Humboldt is a subteam of Flex Trading Enablement (Trading Optimisation). We sit at the intersection of commercial energy trading and the green transition, and we own Asset Backed Trading.
Asset Backed Trading went live in March 2026. It already runs in two countries, with more markets and features on the way. There is a lot of room to shape how it is built.
It models trading, ancillary service allocation, and dispatch for EU portfolios of batteries, solar and wind. We take market and position updates from Flex APIs, allocate energy and services that help stabilise the grid such as FCR and aFRR across the portfolio, and disaggregate those decisions to individual sites. We can both help traders make decisions about how to trade, and disaggregate said trades into per-asset dispatch decisions.
This is production software with genuine commercial and operational impact. It not only support key traders' workflows, but also it drives physical asset dispatch and the delivery of grid services, so we care a lot about getting it right. You will work with data scientists and traders to turn prototypes into reliable, well tested services they can trust.

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join Humboldt and help shape Asset Backed Trading as it grows into new countries and capabilities.
You will work in a Python monorepo of serverless services: event driven pipelines that ingest market and asset data, build optimisation problems, call solvers, and write dispatch and trading positions back out. You will also help evolve the interfaces with other Flex services and APIs that Asset Backed Trading depends on.

React de cara al cliente. No necesitas ser el referente de front, pero sí construir features completas y sostener las convenciones del squad.
Clean Architecture aplicada, no leída. Inversión de control, dominio aislado de la infraestructura, el tecnologías específicas como piezas desechables: arquitectura evolutiva de verdad.
Testing como parte del entregable. Cobertura unitaria más tests de integración que levantan las piezas del caso de uso, con terceros simulados. Acá no hay QA: cada equipo prueba hasta donde el riesgo quede manejado.
Diagnóstico de performance e incidentes. Leer señales de la aplicación —observabilidad, trazas, métricas— y concluir qué dicen del software. La base de datos es un caso concreto: leer el plan de ejecución en vez de adivinarlo, índices, escaneos de tabla.
Tomar cualquier tarea técnica del producto, de punta a punta. React en el front de cara al cliente, .NET en el backend y Python en los servicios que ese backend consume. No entras a cubrir un hueco de tecnología: entras para que el squad pueda avanzar en los tres frentes a la vez, sin mayor acompañamiento.
Mandar a producción rápido para aprender del uso real. Valoramos llegar a tiempo al mercado, así que muchas decisiones se toman sabiendo que dejan deuda. Cada sprint reserva un espacio que planifica el propio equipo para robustecer lo que ya se validó como core: distinguir qué deuda se paga y cuál se deja viva es parte del rol.
Desarrollar con agentes y con contención. Vamos hacia un enfoque agéntico antes que de supervisión humana, y eso se sostiene con tests y restricciones alrededor de lo que hace el agente, no con fe.
Compartir el objetivo de negocio. El norte es el mismo para todo el squad: quienes vienen del lado de producto y quienes vienen del lado técnico persiguen el mismo resultado. Entiendes la tesis de negocio detrás de un requerimiento antes de implementarlo, y descartas rápido lo que no funciona.
Construir para el Maxxa que viene. Ya operamos en México y estamos evaluando el próximo país. El segmento al que apunta este producto —la empresa chica, la que nadie financia— es el mismo en toda la región, y lo que validemos acá es lo que se lleva.
Sostener el estándar sin autoridad formal. El producto se apoya en servicios que construyen otros equipos de Tecnología. No los diriges: los alineas, con criterio propio sobre qué aceptas recibir.
Cómo se ve que vas bien. Tomas tareas de complejidad creciente sin acompañamiento, los flujos que tocas quedan con su cobertura de tests y empiezas a proponer qué se robustece. Eso es lo que miramos, y se conversa contigo desde el primer día.
Haber construido en un producto en validación de mercado , no solo en líneas maduras y estables.
Haber aprendido un stack o tecnología nueva sobre la marcha y haber llegado a ser productivo rápido en ella.

OverviewVisual Studio Code is where millions of developers turn ideas into working software. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer in Zurich to help build its next generation of editing, development, and GitHub Copilot experiences.

You will help make complex developer workflows feel simple, from everyday coding and debugging to delegating work to AI. This is hands-on product engineering in a large TypeScript and Rust codebase: you will shape a feature or technical area-s direction, implement it, and keep improving it after release.

We value engineers who care about how software feels, make sound decisions amid ambiguity, and learn from what they ship. About the teamWe work in the open, with direct feedback from developers and extension authors. You will collaborate with engineers, designers, researchers, and product teams across our team, GitHub, and Microsoft.

We combine community feedback, research, experiments, and engineering judgment to decide what to build. Performance, accessibility, extensibility, security, and developer control are part of the product, not finishing touches.

Examples of workThe role spans core VS Code and Copilot; illustrative projects include: Improve navigation and editing in large repositories without slowing down startup or typing. Build a Copilot workflow that helps developers delegate a coding task, inspect the changes, and validate them using VS Code-s review, testing, and debugging tools.

Extend VS Code APIs so new capabilities work reliably with existing extensions and remote development environments. Refine our existing engineering process with custom tools fine-tuned for throughput and quality.

Responsibilities Identify product and engineering opportunities, helping define what to build through user feedback, experimentation, and technical insight. Shape technical direction within your area, balancing near-term product needs with long-term maintainability.

Lead hands-on design, implementation, testing, and delivery of VS Code features, coordinating contributors and partner-team dependencies as needed. Own outcomes after release: understand adoption, investigate quality issues, and use telemetry, evaluations, and user feedback to guide improvements.

Improve responsiveness and reliability through profiling, debugging, and automated testing; strengthen the tools that let the team experiment and ship confidently. Work in the open: discuss designs publicly, investigate community-reported issues, and collaborate directly with developers and extension authors.

Mentor engineers and improve technical decisions through constructive design and code reviews.

QualificationsBasic Qualifications: Bachelor-s Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 4+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C\#, Java, JavaScript, or Python OR equivalent experience.

Solid programming and application engineering skills, with the ability to become productive in a large TypeScript and Rust codebase. Experience leading technical design and hands-on delivery for complex projects involving multiple contributors, within one team or across partner teams.

Sound product and engineering judgment, including the ability to turn an ambiguous user problem into a practical, maintainable solution. Solid communication and collaboration skills, including working across team boundaries and helping other engineers grow.

Preferred QualificationsWe welcome a range of product backgrounds; these are helpful experiences, not a checklist. Previous work on developer tools, open-source projects, or AI products is not required.
